σφωέ , dual nom. and acc. of the Pron. of 3rd pers., of which the gen. sg. and nom. pl. are οὗ, σφεῖς (qq. v.); dat. σφωΐν:—
A.they two, both of them, only masc. and fem., and always enclit., Il. 1.8 , al.; strengthd., “σφωΐν ἀμφοτέροιιν”
Od. 20.327
:—the form σφώ is only found in post-Homeric Ep. , as Antim. 9.11 (in Il. 17.531
σφω᾽ Αἴαντε is the best reading, cf. A.D. Pron. 88.24 , Hdn.Gr. 2.72 ).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
